body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES"
  title: "Authority-fact projection surfaces: CLI command + MCP tool (the MCP tool is a frozen-catalog change across three repos)"
  epic: "consequence gating"
  component: "Audit / Evidence"
  module: "audit-integrity"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  dependencies:
    - "ISSUE-AUTHORITY-FACT-PROJECTION (#1001) — domain + re-derivation verification, LANDED"
    - "rigorix-sdk: catalog method (filed separately)"
    - "rigorix-enterprise: ingestion + console (filed separately)"

  intent: |
    Make the authority-fact projection reachable: a CLI command to emit a bundle,
    and an MCP tool so it is available over the governed surface. The two halves
    have very different costs and must not be conflated — the CLI is our own
    surface (contained), while the MCP tool changes the FROZEN catalog and is
    therefore a cross-repo contract change.

  in_scope:
    - "CLI: a command that emits an AuthorityFactBundle (projection + history + subjects)"
    - "CLI: a verify subcommand applying the re-derivation check, so the check is runnable"
    - "Decision + design for the MCP tool name, schema and auth level (frozen catalog)"
    - "If the tool is added: mcp descriptor + host routing + server catalog parity + conformance"

  out_of_scope:
    - "The projection domain/application code and the re-derivation verifier (landed in #1001)"
    - "The SDK catalog edit itself (needs its own issue and release; filed in rigorix-sdk)"
    - "Enterprise console rendering (filed in rigorix-enterprise)"
    - "A signed projection (documented as deferred in spec 4.3.2)"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "No change (landed in #1001)"
    application:
      - "Expose ProjectAuthorityFacts + verify_authority_fact_bundle through a CLI-facing service if not already reachable"
    infrastructure:
      - "History read for the bundle (reuse the anchored history reader)"
    api:
      - "New: CLI subcommand(s)"
      - "New (decision required): MCP tool descriptor + routing — a FROZEN catalog change"

  canonical_references:
    - module: "docs/spec/consequence-gating-v1.md#431-verification-shall-be-by-re-derivation-not-by-signature"
    - module: "docs/spec/consequence-gating-v1.md#432-a-signed-projection-is-a-permitted-optimisation-with-a-condition"
    - adr:
        - ".pi/architecture/decisions/ADR-016-audit-integrity-anchor.md"
        - ".pi/architecture/decisions/ADR-017-consequence-gating.md"
    - last_sync: "2026-10-12"

  acceptance_criteria:
    - "A CLI command emits a bundle that a third party can verify by re-derivation"
    - "A CLI verify subcommand applies the re-derivation check and exits non-zero on failure"
    - "The output carries no absolute path, username or secret (spec NC + ADR-017 redaction)"
    - "If an MCP tool is added: the name is added to the SDK catalog contract FIRST, then both servers, then conformance"
    - "Catalog parity tests (OSS server + SDK conformance) are updated in the same change set"
    - "validate-ci.sh / validate-tests.sh / validate-canonical.sh pass"

  validators:
    - ci
    - tests
    - architecture
    - canonical

  implementation_notes: |
    ## Do the CLI first; treat the MCP tool as a separate, gated decision

    The CLI is our own surface and blocks nothing. The MCP tool is a frozen-catalog
    change with this actual shape (measured 2026-10-12):

      SDK  schemas/api/catalog.json                      -> 23 methods (canonical)
           python/rigorix_verifier/_schemas/api/          -> 23 (copy)
           typescript/_schemas/api/                       -> 23 (copy)
      OSS  server/src/mcp_http.rs:529                     -> assert_eq!(exposed.len(), 17)
           server/tests/catalog_parity.rs                -> names == CATALOG.len()

    So adding one method means, in order:

      1. rigorix-sdk  — the canonical catalog + both polyglot copies + conformance
                        fixtures (a minor SDK release; verifiers must accept the
                        new method set)
      2. rigorix-oss  — mcp descriptor + routing, then server parity/conformance
      3. enterprise   — ingestion/console if it surfaces the tool

    That sequencing is not optional: a verifier built against the old catalog will
    reject or ignore the new method, exactly as the 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 attribution
    sequencing bit us before.

    ## Is a tool the right surface at all?

    Worth deciding explicitly rather than by default. The projection is an EXPORT
    for an external determination consumer or an auditor, not a step an agent takes
    mid-run. Arguments for the tool: reachability over the governed surface,
    consistent auth (`AuthLevel`), and it reuses the existing audit tool plumbing.
    Arguments against: it widens the agent-visible surface for something that is
    fundamentally an offline artifact, and it costs a three-repo contract change.

    If it is added, note the disclosure property in the tool description: a bundle
    carries the ENVELOPES, so a caller receives the history, not just a summary.
    That is inherent to the re-derivation design (spec 4.3.1) and should be stated,
    not discovered.

    ## Redaction

    Reuse the ADR-017 redaction helpers. The projection is explicitly shared with
    auditors, so an absolute path or username leak is a real disclosure. The
    existing test `no_absolute_paths_or_username_in_the_canonical_bytes` covers the
    projection; the CLI must not add a leak in its own output (e.g. echoing the
    store path).

  file_changes:
    - "modify: cli/src/cli_boundary/cli.rs (new subcommand)"
    - "modify: cli/src/cli_boundary/orchestrator.rs (dispatch)"
    - "create: cli/src/cli_boundary/tests (bundle emit + verify subcommand)"
    - "modify (only if the tool is approved): mcp/src/audit_tools/interfaces/mcp/mod.rs"
    - "modify (only if the tool is approved): mcp/src/host/mod.rs (routing)"
    - "modify (only if the tool is approved): server/tests/catalog_parity.rs"

  pipeline_steps:
    - implement
    - validate
    - create-mr
    - merge
---

# ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES — make the projection reachable

## Intent

`#1001` landed the projection domain, the bundle and the re-derivation verifier,
but nothing can reach them:

```
grep -rln 'ProjectAuthorityFacts|AuthorityFactBundle' cli/src mcp/src
  → (empty)
```

This issue makes them reachable. The CLI half is contained; the MCP half is a
three-repo contract change and is called out as such rather than bundled in.

## Dependencies

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ISSUE-AUTHORITY-FACT-PROJECTION      │  LANDED (d9e4b7c3)
│ domain + bundle + re-derivation      │
└───────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ISSUE-PROJECTION-SURFACES            │ ← THIS ISSUE
│ CLI (contained) · MCP (frozen)       │
└───────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                │ MCP half requires:
                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ rigorix-sdk: catalog method          │  (filed separately)
│ rigorix-enterprise: ingest + console │  (filed separately)
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## In Scope

- CLI command emitting a bundle.
- CLI verify subcommand applying the re-derivation check.
- The MCP tool decision **and** design (name, schema, auth level).

## Out of Scope

- The projection domain/application and verifier (landed).
- The SDK catalog edit (separate repo and release).
- Enterprise console rendering (separate repo).
- A signed projection (spec 4.3.2, deferred with conditions).

## The frozen-catalog cost (measured)

| repo | artifact | current |
|---|---|---|
| SDK | `schemas/api/catalog.json` (canonical) | 23 methods |
| SDK | `python/…/_schemas/api/catalog.json`, `typescript/_schemas/api/` | 23 (copies) |
| OSS | `server/src/mcp_http.rs:529` | `assert_eq!(exposed.len(), 17)` |
| OSS | `server/tests/catalog_parity.rs` | `names == CATALOG.len()` |

Ordering is load-bearing: **SDK catalog first**, then both servers, then
conformance — a verifier built against the old catalog will not accept the new
method, which is exactly how the 0.3.0→0.4.0 attribution sequencing went wrong.

## Question worth answering explicitly

Is an MCP **tool** the right surface for this? The projection is an export for an
external consumer or auditor, not a step an agent takes mid-run. It reuses the
governed surface and auth, but it widens the agent-visible surface for something
fundamentally offline, and it costs a three-repo contract change. The CLI may be
the whole answer.

If the tool is added, its description must state that a bundle carries the
**envelopes** — the caller receives the history, not a summary. That is inherent to
re-derivation (spec 4.3.1) and should be declared, not discovered.

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion | Validator |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | CLI emits a bundle verifiable by re-derivation | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 2 | CLI verify exits non-zero on a failed check | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 3 | No absolute path / username / secret in CLI output | `validate-security.sh` |
| 4 | If MCP: SDK catalog updated first, then OSS, then conformance | `validate-canonical.sh` |
| 5 | If MCP: catalog parity + conformance updated in one change set | `validate-ci.sh` |

## Implementation

> **Agent:** Implement the CLI first and land it. Do not start the MCP tool until
> the SDK catalog method exists — the parity tests will fail otherwise, and that
> is by design.

### Steps

1. Add the CLI subcommand to `cli.rs` and dispatch it in `orchestrator.rs`
2. Emit the bundle (projection + envelopes + subjects) via the existing serializer
3. Add a verify subcommand calling `verify_authority_fact_bundle`, non-zero on error
4. Assert redaction in the CLI output (reuse the ADR-017 helpers)
5. Decide the MCP question; if yes, design name/schema/auth level and file the SDK dependency
6. Only after the SDK catalog lands: mcp descriptor + routing + parity
7. Run all validators
title: Authority-fact projection surfaces: CLI command + MCP tool (the MCP tool is a frozen-catalog change across three repos)

---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-FLAKY-SCHEMA-CACHE-STALENESS"
  title: "Flaky test: mcp test_schema_cache_is_stale asserts on a zero-duration window, so it races the clock"
  epic: "tooling / test reliability"
  component: "MCP / Audit Tools"
  module: "audit-tools"
  status: planned
  priority: low
  dependencies: []

  intent: |
    Remove a genuine flake. `test_schema_cache_is_stale` calls
    `is_stale(Duration::seconds(0))` immediately after `update()`, which requires
    the clock to have advanced since the update. If no time elapses (fast machine,
    coarse clock resolution, or an implementation that compares with `>=`), the
    assertion fails for reasons unrelated to the behaviour under test.

  in_scope:
    - "Make the staleness test deterministic (inject the clock, or test the boundary without racing wall time)"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Changing the staleness semantics themselves (the max-age contract stays)"
    - "Auditing other tests for flakiness (separate, if it recurs)"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "Modified: SchemaCache staleness boundary (only if it takes an injected clock)"
    application:
      - "No change"
    infrastructure:
      - "No change"
    api:
      - "No change"

  canonical_references:
    - module: "mcp/src/audit_tools (schema cache)"
    - last_sync: "2026-10-12"

  acceptance_criteria:
    - "The test no longer depends on wall-clock advance between two statements"
    - "The max-age boundary is still tested (a zero window is stale, a large window is not)"
    - "The test passes repeatedly in the full suite (not only in isolation)"

  validators:
    - ci
    - tests

  implementation_notes: |
    Observed during verification of PR #1003: the test failed once in a full run
    and then passed 5/5 in isolation — the classic signature of a timing
    dependency rather than a product bug. It is pre-existing, unrelated to that PR.

    Current shape (mcp/tests/enterprise_proxy_contract_freeze_test.rs):

        cache.update(metadata);
        assert!(!cache.is_stale(chrono::Duration::seconds(3600)));
        assert!(cache.is_stale(chrono::Duration::seconds(0)));   // <- races the clock

    The last line requires `elapsed > 0`. It is true only if the clock advanced
    between `update()` and the assertion.

    Prefer injecting the clock (a `now` parameter or a test clock) so the boundary
    is exercised without racing real time. If `is_stale` compares with `>` rather
    than `>=`, note that in the fix — the zero-window case is exactly where the two
    differ, and the test is unintentionally pinning that choice.

  file_changes:
    - "modify: mcp/src/audit_tools (schema cache staleness, if the clock is injected)"
    - "modify: mcp/tests/enterprise_proxy_contract_freeze_test.rs"

  pipeline_steps:
    - implement
    - validate
    - create-mr
    - merge
---

# ISSUE-FLAKY-SCHEMA-CACHE-STALENESS — a test that races the clock

## Problem

`mcp/tests/enterprise_proxy_contract_freeze_test.rs`:

```rust
#[test]
fn test_schema_cache_is_stale() {
    let mut cache = SchemaCache::new();

    // Empty cache is always stale
    assert!(cache.is_stale(chrono::Duration::seconds(1)));

    let metadata = EnterpriseMetadata { /* ... */ };
    cache.update(metadata);

    // Just updated — should not be stale
    assert!(!cache.is_stale(chrono::Duration::hours(1)));
    assert!(!cache.is_stale(chrono::Duration::seconds(3600)));

    // Already elapsed — stale
    assert!(cache.is_stale(chrono::Duration::seconds(0)));   // <- needs elapsed > 0
}
```

The final assertion asserts that a cache updated microseconds ago is stale under a
**zero** max-age. That is only true if the clock has advanced since `update()`. On
a fast machine, or with coarser clock resolution, no time elapses and the test
fails — reporting a product bug that does not exist.

## Evidence

Observed in the PR #1003 verification run: failed once in the full suite, then
passed 5/5 in isolation. Pre-existing; unrelated to that PR. Recorded here so it is
not mistaken later for a regression in whatever PR happens to trigger it.

## Fix

Inject the clock (a `now` parameter or a test clock) so the boundary is exercised
without racing wall time. While fixing it, note whether `is_stale` compares with
`>` or `>=` — the zero-window case is precisely where they differ, so this test is
currently pinning that choice implicitly rather than stating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion | Validator |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | No dependency on elapsed wall time between two statements | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 2 | The max-age boundary is still covered (zero → stale, large → fresh) | `validate-tests.sh` |
| 3 | Passes repeatedly in a full run, not only in isolation | `validate-ci.sh` |

## Implementation

> **Agent:** This is a test-determinism fix, not a behaviour change. Do not alter
> the staleness contract — only how the test establishes "time has passed".

### Steps

1. Read the `SchemaCache` staleness implementation and note `>` vs `>=`
2. Inject the clock (or take `now` as a parameter) where the boundary is decided
3. Rewrite the test to advance the injected clock instead of racing real time
4. Keep both boundary assertions (zero window stale, large window fresh)
5. Run the full mcp suite repeatedly to confirm the flake is gone
title: Flaky test: mcp test_schema_cache_is_stale asserts on a zero-duration window, so it races the clock

body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-VALIDATOR-SINGLE-SOURCE"
  title: "The mirrored .pi/scripts validators have no single source of truth — five trees have drifted into 2–4 variants each"
  epic: "tooling / ci integrity"
  component: "CI / Validators"
  module: "validator-tooling"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  dependencies:
    - "461ea2b9 (cwd resolution preamble — already landed, fixes a different defect)"

  intent: |
    Establish one source of truth for the validator scripts that are mirrored into
    every crate tree, so that `bash engine/.pi/scripts/validate-tests.sh` and
    `bash mcp/.pi/scripts/validate-tests.sh` are the same program — or, where a
    per-tree difference is intentional, record it explicitly and enforce it.

    This issue is deliberately NOT "make all copies byte-identical". That was
    attempted and reverted; see the warning section. The drift is real, but some
    per-tree differences are legitimate and a blanket normalisation makes things
    worse.

  in_scope:
    - "Inventory which mirrored files are (a) substantively drifted, (b) cosmetically drifted, (c) intentionally per-tree"
    - "Reconcile the substantively-drifted rust validators to one implementation"
    - "A guard that FAILS on unintentional drift, so it cannot recur silently"
    - "Fix the hardcoded 'language: C.UTF-8' message (35 dispatcher files)"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Rewriting the non-rust language validators: every tree is Rust, so languages/{go,java,python,typescript}/* never execute here. Their drift is cosmetic and inert."
    - "Changing which validators exist per tree (engine's validate-code-graph-contracts.sh, server having none, guards being root-only are all intentional)"
    - "Cross-repo deduplication with rigorix-sdk — tracked separately"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "No code change — tooling"
    application:
      - "No code change"
    infrastructure:
      - "Modified: the rust validator implementations, reconciled from the newest variant"
      - "Modified: .pi/scripts/validate-*.sh dispatchers (the C.UTF-8 message)"
      - "New: a drift guard wired into a gating path"

  canonical_references:
    - module: ".pi/guards.tsv"
    - adr: []
    - last_sync: "2026-10-12"

  acceptance_criteria:
    - "The substantively-drifted rust validators have ONE implementation each, shared or byte-identical by construction"
    - "A gating guard fails when a mirrored file drifts, and prints which trees disagree"
    - "Intentional per-tree differences are recorded (which file, which trees, why) so the guard can distinguish drift from design"
    - "The 'language: C.UTF-8' message prints the detected language"
    - "Every per-tree validator still passes when invoked from the repo root in the form the hardening loop uses"
    - "validate-ci.sh / validate-guards.sh pass"

  validators:
    - ci
    - tests
    - architecture

  implementation_notes: |
    ## WARNING — do not blanket-normalise (this was tried and reverted)

    An attempt was made to make every mirrored file identical across all trees.
    It was reverted because it did two harmful things:

    1. It rewrote 20 files under `languages/{go,java,python,typescript}/` whose
       differences were COSMETIC (`|| true` additions, a `LANG` -> `LANG_DETECTED`
       rename) and which are INERT — every tree is Rust, so `detect_language`
       returns `rust` and those files never execute. Checksum-matching dead files
       is churn, not a fix.
    2. It copied the four security guards (`validate-guards.sh`,
       `validate-panic-sites.sh`, `validate-secret-logs.sh`,
       `validate-unsafe-sites.sh`) into every tree. Those scripts resolve
       `.pi/panic-baseline.tsv` and friends relative to a tree, so the copies would
       have run against baselines that do not exist there — breaking the very
       guards, and making the hardening discovery loop run each of them 5x.

    Treat "hashes differ" as a QUESTION, not a verdict. Drift is only a defect
    where the difference is substantive AND the file executes.

    ## What is actually drifted (measured 2026-10-12)

    Mirrored in 5 trees (ROOT, engine, mcp, cli, actions); server has no
    dispatchers at all.

    Rust validators — variants across the 5 trees:
      tests         4 variants   <- substantive
      ci            3 variants   <- substantive
      integration   3 variants   <- substantive
      architecture  2 variants   <- substantive
      canonical     2 variants   <- substantive
      operations    1 variant    <- already consistent
      security      1 variant    <- already consistent (fixed earlier)

    Dispatcher sets per tree: ROOT 13, engine 10, mcp 9, cli 9, actions 9,
    server 0. Different SETS, not just different content — and that may be
    intentional, so map it before changing it.

    ## The substantive differences (these are the fix)

    - `validate-tests.sh`: ROOT uses `cargo tarpaulin`; engine uses
      `cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 80`. Different tool, different result.
    - `validate-integration.sh`: some trees call `cargo test --test '*'`, which
      ERRORS on a target declaring `required-features` (a false failure); others
      call `cargo test --tests`, which skips such targets. The fix exists in some
      trees only.
    - `validate-ci.sh`: engine scopes with `-p rigorix-{crate}`; mcp has an ad-hoc
      `cd mcp` hack; ROOT has neither.
    - `validate-architecture.sh`: engine detects per-module layers
      (`src/{module}/domain/`) and accepts a flat/thin crate; ROOT only checks
      root-level `src/domain` and FAILS a thin crate.

    ## Real bug found while gathering this

    35 dispatcher files across the 5 trees print:

        echo "No <x> validator for language: C.UTF-8"

    `C.UTF-8` is a locale, not a language. This is a `$LANG` that was expanded to
    its value at edit time; the message should name the detected language. (Note
    also that one variant assigns `LANG=$(detect_language)`, shadowing the locale
    environment variable — prefer `LANG_DETECTED`.)

    ## Already fixed, do not redo

    The cwd-sensitivity defect (validators reading `src/` relative to the caller's
    cwd, so they failed or silently PASSED while skipping work when run from the
    repo root) was fixed in 461ea2b9 by resolving the tree from the script's own
    path, and the CI integration job now runs the per-crate copies.

    ## Cross-repo note

    `rigorix-sdk` carries the same seven `languages/rust/validate-*.sh` files and
    all seven differ from OSS. Filed separately in that repo; do not try to fix it
    from here.

  file_changes:
    - "modify: .pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-*.sh (reconcile the substantive drift)"
    - "modify: */​.pi/scripts/languages/rust/validate-*.sh (same implementation)"
    - "modify: .pi/scripts/validate-*.sh and per-tree copies (the C.UTF-8 message)"
    - "create: .pi/scripts/validate-script-drift.sh (+ a recorded intentional-difference list)"

  pipeline_steps:
    - implement
    - validate
    - create-mr
    - merge
---

# ISSUE-VALIDATOR-SINGLE-SOURCE — mirrored validators have drifted

## Intent

`.pi/scripts` is mirrored into every crate tree. The validator implementations
inside it have drifted apart, so the same command name means a different program
depending on which tree you invoke it from.

The goal is **one source of truth**, plus a guard so drift cannot recur silently —
not "make every file identical", which is both wrong and already reverted once.

## Evidence (measured 2026-10-12)

| rust validator | variants across 5 trees | nature |
|---|---|---|
| `validate-tests.sh` | **4** | substantive (`tarpaulin` vs `llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 80`) |
| `validate-ci.sh` | **3** | substantive (per-crate `-p rigorix-{crate}` scoping vs a `cd mcp` hack vs neither) |
| `validate-integration.sh` | **3** | substantive (`--test '*'` errors on `required-features` targets; `--tests` is the fix) |
| `validate-architecture.sh` | **2** | substantive (module layers + flat-crate acceptance vs root-only, which FAILS thin crates) |
| `validate-canonical.sh` | **2** | substantive (`SRC_DIR`/`PI_DIR` fallback + module-name matching) |
| `validate-operations.sh` | 1 | consistent |
| `validate-security.sh` | 1 | consistent (fixed earlier) |

Dispatcher sets also differ by tree — ROOT 13, engine 10, mcp 9, cli 9, actions 9,
server 0 — and **that may be intentional**, so map before changing.

## Warning — the trap

A blanket normalisation was attempted and reverted. It:

1. rewrote 20 **inert, cosmetically-different** files under
   `languages/{go,java,python,typescript}/` (every tree is Rust; those never run);
2. copied the four security guards into every tree, where they would resolve
   `.pi/panic-baseline.tsv` against baselines that don't exist — breaking the
   guards and multiplying each of them 5x in the discovery loop.

**"Hashes differ" is a question, not a verdict.** Drift is a defect only where the
difference is substantive *and* the file executes.

## Also here

35 dispatcher files print `language: C.UTF-8` — a `$LANG` expanded at edit time
instead of the detected language. Small, real, and trivially fixed. (One variant
also assigns `LANG=`, shadowing the locale env var; prefer `LANG_DETECTED`.)

## Out of scope

- The non-rust language validators (inert here).
- Changing which validators exist per tree.
- Cross-repo dedup with `rigorix-sdk` (filed there).

## Acceptance Criteria

| # | Criterion | Validator |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | Substantively-drifted rust validators have one implementation | `validate-ci.sh` |
| 2 | A gating guard fails on unintentional drift and names the disagreeing trees | `validate-guards.sh` |
| 3 | Intentional per-tree differences are recorded, so the guard distinguishes drift from design | review |
| 4 | The `C.UTF-8` message prints the detected language | `validate-ci.sh` |
| 5 | Every per-tree validator still passes when invoked as the hardening loop invokes it | `validate-integration.sh` |

## Implementation

> **Agent:** Read the warning section first. Measure which differences are
> substantive before touching anything, and record intentional differences before
> adding the guard — otherwise the guard will fail on design.

### Steps

1. Re-measure the variant matrix per tree (do not trust the table above; it ages)
2. Classify every difference: substantive / cosmetic / intentional
3. Reconcile only the substantive ones, from the newest variant
4. Fix the `C.UTF-8` message (and prefer `LANG_DETECTED` over `LANG`)
5. Record intentional per-tree differences in a list the guard reads
6. Add `validate-script-drift.sh` and register it in `.pi/guards.tsv` as gating
7. Verify each per-tree copy from the repo root; run `validate-guards.sh`
title: The mirrored .pi/scripts validators have no single source of truth — five trees drifted into 2–4 variants each

body:
---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-AUTHORITY-FACT-PROJECTION"
  title: "Authority-fact projection: a third-party-verifiable export of signed history as attributable present-state facts"
  epic: "consequence gating"
  component: "Audit / Evidence"
  module: "audit-integrity"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  dependencies:
    - "ADR-016 audit integrity anchor (anchored mode)"
    - "ADR-017 evidence redaction (no absolute paths in signed records)"
    - "SDK 0.4.0 published verifiers (rust / python / typescript)"
    - "ISSUE-PRECONDITION-PROVIDERS (consumer of this output)"

  intent: |
    Produce a signed, offline-verifiable projection of Rigorix's own hash-chained
    history as attributable present-state facts: what authority was checked, when,
    with what outcome, with what digests, and at what chain position. The purpose is
    to be the PRODUCER of verifiable facts for an external determination consumer —
    a consumer that is explicitly forbidden from treating its own runtime packet as
    provenance — without asserting present standing itself.

# ISSUE-AUTHORITY-FACT-PROJECTION — our records as attributable facts

## Intent

Rigorix already holds the thing an external determination consumer says it needs:
signed, hash-chained records that a third party can verify **without running the
engine and without the operator's key** (anchored mode, ADR-016). This issue
exposes that as a deliberate output — a *fact projection* — rather than leaving it
as an internal audit trail.

The strategic point: the counterpart's own contract requires verifiable provenance
and forbids it from treating a runtime packet as its own evidence. We are a
legitimate source of such evidence for authority state specifically. That makes us
the producer of its input, which is a stronger and simpler position than asking it
to route execution through us.

## Why not assert standing

Because asserting standing is not our jurisdiction and would be an overclaim we
could not defend. Our claim is narrower and stronger:

> "At chain position N, authority X for scope S was checked at time T, the check
> artifact had digest D, and the outcome was O. Here is the anchor that lets you
> verify none of that was altered."

Whether that constitutes *present* standing is the consumer's determination. We
supply facts with provenance; they supply the judgement. That split is the same
discipline that already governs our own evidence (the `recorded` /
`refused_before_check` / `artifact_unreadable` distinction exists precisely so that
absences are not overloaded).

## Dependencies

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ADR-016 anchor + hash-chained audit │  EXISTS
│  offline verifiers (rust/py/ts)      │  PUBLISHED
└───────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                │
                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ISSUE-AUTHORITY-FACT-PROJECTION     │ ← THIS ISSUE (producer)
└───────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                │  attributable present-state facts
                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ISSUE-PRECONDITION-PROVIDERS        │  (consumer side)
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## In Scope

- A projection for identity + scope + time window.
- Provenance on every fact: attributable source, established_at, evidence refs.
- Epistemic status that preserves UNKNOWN distinctly.
- Chain position + anchor reference (independently checkable).
- Offline verification by the published verifiers.
- A machine-readable claim ceiling.
- Redaction at construction.

## Out of Scope

- Asserting present standing.
- Becoming an authority of record for identity or delegation legality.
- New keys or trust roots.
- Guaranteeing the operator's authority artifact is externally true — we record
  what was checked, not that the world matches it.
